1. Introduction

Competitive programming (CP) is an essential discipline for computer science students seeking to master algorithmic efficiency, discrete mathematics, and high-performance problem solving. However, active contestants constantly struggle with disjointed workflows across competing platforms like Codeforces, LeetCode, CodeChef, and AtCoder. Contestants lack a unified platform to track cross-judge ratings, analyze contest failures, and systematically practice neglected problem categories.

CodeArena is an advanced, native Android mobile application engineered entirely in Pure Java to solve these productivity hurdles. Designed specifically as an end-to-end training and contest companion, CodeArena combines live multi-platform contest tracking, exact alarm scheduling, an ongoing Foreground Service stopwatch, a personalized Generative AI performance coach (Google Gemini 1.5 Pro), and an offline repository of 381 curated algorithm tutorials.

2. Objectives and Scope

The primary objectives of the CodeArena project are:

  • Multi-Platform Profile Aggregator: Provide a unified dashboard that syncs and visualizes ratings, badges, and solve counts from Codeforces, LeetCode, CodeChef, AtCoder, and HackerRank.
  • Contest Scheduling & Exact Reminders: Aggregate global contests from CLIST.by and Codeforces APIs, scheduling exact alarms that survive device reboots via AlarmManager and BootReceiver.
  • Virtual Contest Simulation: Emulate timed contest conditions using a non-killable Android ForegroundService with live status-bar notification controls.
  • AI-Powered Diagnostics: Leverage the Google Gemini 1.5 Pro REST API to analyze contest performance and provide progressive algorithmic hints without spoiling complete solutions.
  • Algorithmic Mastery: Track topic mastery across 100-rating intervals (800–900, 1000–1100, etc.) for dynamic programming, graphs, math, and greedy algorithms.
  • Offline Educational Catalog: Bundle 381 Codeforces tutorials with full mathematical notation (LaTeX/MathML) for distraction-free learning.
  • Academic Excellence: Adhere 100% to the CSE 2200: Advanced Programming Laboratory curriculum by implementing pure Java OOP, Room SQLite, Retrofit/OkHttp, Services, Broadcast Receivers, Content Providers, and App Widgets.

3. Technology Stack and Architecture

CodeArena adopts a modern Model-View-ViewModel (MVVM) architecture with clean separation between the presentation layer, repository domain, and underlying local/remote data sources.

Component Technology / Library Implementation Purpose
Programming Language Pure Java (Java 8/17) Full adherence to CSE 2200 syllabus without Kotlin dependencies.
IDE & Build System Android Studio, Gradle (KTS) Compilation, debugging, dependency management, and APK packaging.
User Interface Material Design, ViewBinding Dark-themed responsive UI, ConstraintLayout, and fluid RecyclerViews.
Local Database Room SQLite (9 Entities, 9 DAOs) Offline caching of contests, problems, runs, tag XP, and AI responses.
Networking & Parsing Retrofit 2, OkHttp 3, Gson REST API communication, rate-limit interception, and JSON mapping.
Generative AI Google Gemini 1.5 Pro REST API Automated contest analysis, hint generation, and debriefing.
Authentication Firebase Auth, Google Sign-In Email/password and Google OAuth with account storage isolation.
Background Service Android Foreground Service Persistent virtual contest stopwatch with ongoing notification.
Event & Alarm Handling BroadcastReceiver, AlarmManager Exact contest reminders, boot rescheduling, notification clicks.
Inter-App Provider ContentProvider, FileProvider External access to contest tables and secure result-card image sharing.
Desktop Widget AppWidgetProvider Interactive home-screen widget displaying the daily challenge problem.

The application cleanly encapsulates business logic into repository classes (CodeforcesRepository, ContestRepository, UserPreferencesRepository, CatalogRepository). ViewModels expose asynchronous data through reactive LiveData streams, ensuring zero UI thread blocking during intensive database queries and REST requests.

4.6 Spaced-Repetition Upsolve System

Automatically tracks problems that a contestant failed to solve during virtual or live rounds. The system queues the problem across increasing review intervals (Day 1, Day 3, Day 7, Day 14, Day 30) using the Leitner flashcard methodology.

↓

↓
Step 5: Advance Review Stage to Next Interval (Day 3 → Day 7 → Day 14)

6. API and Backend Integration

6.1 Codeforces REST API

The application utilizes Retrofit 2 with Gson converter to communicate with Codeforces REST endpoints:

  • user.info?handles={handle}: Fetches profile avatar, global rank, rating, and organization.
  • user.status?handle={handle}&from=1&count=5000: Extracts complete submission history to compute total accepted problems, verdict breakdowns, and tag distributions.
  • contest.list?gym=false: Retrieves active, upcoming, and past official contests.
  • contest.standings?contestId={id}&from=1&count=100: Downloads contest ranklists to benchmark virtual contest performances.

6.2 CLIST.by Competitive Programming API

CLIST.by aggregates global competitive programming calendars. CodeArena queries upcoming events across Codeforces, LeetCode, CodeChef, and AtCoder with HTTP Basic Authentication headers (api_key and username), caching responses locally in Room SQLite.

6.3 Google Gemini 1.5 Pro AI API

Interactions with the Gemini Pro endpoint (POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-1.5-pro:generateContent) are managed through OkHttp. Performance metrics and failed problem statements are injected into structured prompts, and the returned Markdown response is cached in Room (AiCacheEntity) to eliminate redundant API token consumption.

6.4 Firebase Authentication SDK

Handles user account creation and sign-in via Email/Password and Google OAuth. The authenticated user's UID dynamically isolates local SharedPreferences files (codearena_preferences_<uid>.xml), ensuring multi-user isolation on shared devices.

7. Database Design & Persistence

CodeArena utilizes Android Jetpack Room over SQLite, featuring 9 strongly typed entities with complete DAO interfaces:

Entity Name Primary Key Description & Stored Data
ContestEntity id (Long) Stores contest name, platform, phase, start time, and duration.
ProblemEntity id (Long) Codeforces problem statement, index, rating, tags, and solved state.
VirtualRunEntity id (Auto-inc) Metadata of virtual contest runs (start time, score, penalty, status).
ProblemResultEntity id (Auto-inc) Individual problem submission results and verdicts within a virtual run.
UpsolveItemEntity problemId (String) Spaced repetition intervals (Stages 1 through 5) for failed problems.
NoteEntity id (Auto-inc) Personal algorithmic notes associated with problems or contests.
TagXpEntity tag (String) Accumulated experience points and tier progress per algorithm tag.
AiCacheEntity cacheKey (String) Local cache of Gemini AI responses to avoid duplicate API calls.
RankEstimateEntity contestId (Long) Benchmark percentile data for offline virtual rank estimation.

9. Security, Permissions, and Access Control

  • Runtime Notification Permissions: Automatically requests POST_NOTIFICATIONS on Android 13+ (API 33) to ensure contest reminders and stopwatch alerts post reliably.
  • Exact Alarm Permissions: Declares SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM and USE_EXACT_ALARM to guarantee millisecond-accurate notification delivery.
  • API Key Protection: Sensitive API keys (GEMINI_API_KEY, CLIST_API_KEY) are stored in local.properties and injected at compile time via Gradle BuildConfig, keeping them out of version control.
  • Rate Limiting Protection: Implements RateLimitInterceptor enforcing a 200ms throttle between consecutive API requests, preventing HTTP 429 bans from Codeforces servers.
  • Android 12+ Cloud Auto-Backup: Explicitly configured in data_extraction_rules.xml and backup_rules.xml with BackupManager.dataChanged() hooks, ensuring handles and read tutorial progress survive app reinstallation.

11. Limitations and Future Improvements

  • Automated Code Submission: Direct in-app code submission is currently limited by Cloudflare bot protection on Codeforces. A browser extension bridge or desktop companion daemon could facilitate automated submission in future versions.
  • Multiplayer 1v1 Duels: Expanding the virtual contest simulator into real-time head-to-head battles using Firebase Realtime Database or WebSockets.
  • Built-in Code Editor: Embedding an offline mobile IDE with syntax highlighting and local C++/Java compilation capabilities.

12. Conclusion

CodeArena provides a comprehensive, production-ready competitive programming companion application. By uniting multi-platform profile analytics, exact contest scheduling, an ongoing Foreground Service stopwatch, a personalized Gemini AI mentor, and an offline repository of 381 algorithm tutorials, it eliminates the fragmented workflows of modern competitive programmers.

Engineered strictly in Pure Java, CodeArena demonstrates mastery of every learning objective in the CSE 2200: Advanced Programming Laboratory curriculum—seamlessly combining object-oriented design, multithreaded background processing, Room SQLite persistence, REST networking, and the complete Android component suite.
